patch.value: Ecosystem Daily Release jobs hold a hosted runner for up to 360 minutes waiting on their own release PR's queued CI, and ecosystem CI never cancels superseded runs, so the account's 20 runner slots starve every repository

About 30 ecosystem repositories (pm-rl, pm-ops, pm-presets, pm-swarm, pm-ts-starter, pm-changelog, ...) schedule release.yml at the same cron minute (23 3 * * *, pm-changelog 17 3). Its release job opens a release PR and then waits in-job (merge wait 60-120 minutes, job timeout 360) for that PR's CI, holding a GitHub-hosted runner while the CI it waits for is queued behind the same held runners. Ecosystem ci.yml has no concurrency group, so every push to a PR branch queues another full Node 22/26 (and sometimes Windows) matrix without cancelling the superseded run. All repositories share the personal account's 20 concurrent-job cap, so this starves pm-cli and every other repository for hours. The fix belongs in the ecosystem release and CI templates, not in pm-cli.

No ecosystem release workflow job polls or sleeps for its release PR's checks while holding a runner; publication is triggered by the merge event; Every ecosystem ci.yml declares concurrency group per workflow and ref with cancel-in-progress for pull_request events; Ecosystem release crons are spread over distinct minutes so no two repositories start a release in the same 5-minute window; An account-wide snapshot one hour after the release window shows no in-progress Daily Release run waiting on its own PR
GitHub Free personal account unbraind shared by about 30 public repositories

A daily release never holds a runner while waiting for review or CI: the release job enables auto-merge (or exits) and a separate pull_request closed/workflow_run trigger publishes; ecosystem CI declares concurrency with cancel-in-progress for pull_request refs; release crons are staggered across repositories.

Snapshot 2026-10-30T15:08Z: 60 active workflow runs across the account, 47 queued; 5 Daily Release runs in progress since 10:09-13:37Z all inside 'Run release checks' / merge wait, 7 more queued; pm-ts-starter had 3 CI runs queued for one PR branch (fix/min-sdk-drift-check). pm-cli PR #1629 waited 94 minutes for its first job.

value.text: 2026-10-30 17:15 UTC queue census across all unbraind repos: about 90 queued runs against the 20-job account cap and zero pm-cli jobs in progress. 45 of the queued runs were Dependabot dynamic update jobs, mostly repeats of the same directory update (PersonalAgent pip 10+10, arXiv-PyG-new uv 7, Tokenwerk uv 5). Cancelled the 31 superseded queued Dependabot runs, keeping the newest per repository and directory. Repeated Dependabot update jobs are a second source of runner starvation beside the release merge waits; a durable fix needs grouped Dependabot updates or open-pull-request limits in those repositories.

patch.value: Historical 2026-10-30 starvation observations remain in comments/history. On 2026-11-09 the pm-cli parent 42599219606 waited on independent child 42601586640 for over four hours; only that redundant parent was canceled after verifying the child producer had succeeded. The child and immutable publication identities were preserved. The 16:35 UTC census covered 172 non-archived owner repositories and found ten workflows with sixteen executing Ubuntu jobs, including advancing ordinary CI steps. No unrelated workflow was canceled. Durable decoupling, concurrency and cron changes remain unimplemented under this open owner.

Ecosystem release workflows and the pm-cli exact-tag recovery parent do not hold a runner while waiting for independent PR checks or child workflows. CI concurrency cancels superseded PR runs and ecosystem cron windows are staggered.

Neither ecosystem release jobs nor the pm-cli exact-tag recovery parent hold a hosted runner while waiting for independently dispatched children or queued PR checks; Publication and completion handling use merge or workflow completion events while preserving existing child identity and original failure observations; Ecosystem CI declares workflow-and-ref concurrency with cancellation of superseded pull-request runs; Ecosystem release cron windows are staggered so separate repositories do not begin within the same five-minute window; An account-wide snapshot one hour after a release window finds no ecosystem or pm-cli parent waiting in-job for its own PR checks or child workflow

Runner-held waits occur in both ecosystem release/CI templates and the pm-cli exact-tag recovery parent. Ecosystem daily release jobs have opened a release PR and waited for its queued checks while occupying a hosted runner. The pm-cli Auto Release parent has also waited in-job on an independently dispatched Release child, retaining a runner while the child acceptance jobs were queued. Shared personal-account capacity and uncanceled duplicate CI matrices amplify these waits. Durable remediation must cover both scopes: event-driven publication or observation without a runner-held dependency wait, per-ref PR CI concurrency, and staggered ecosystem cron windows. Ordinary long-running tests are not automatically evidence of a deadlock.

value.text:
Observed again 2026-11-12, during the evening fleet release wave. PR 1714's CI (head 2bbb1c41e, pushed 21:04Z) waited about 60 minutes for its foundation build. Its Ubuntu fan-out jobs, created at 22:04Z, stayed queued until about 23:40Z, and its security jobs, created at 21:04Z, until about 23:30Z.
Censuses:
- 21:30Z: 18 of the 20 account slots were running fleet pull_request CI.
- 23:00Z: 20 of 20 slots were running fleet Ubuntu jobs: release/2026.11.12 PRs on pm-ado, pm-csv and pm-jira; push-to-main CI on pm-github, pm-ts-starter, pm-web and pm-todos; Daily Release runs on pm-ado, pm-vcs and pm-ts-starter; and three feature-branch PRs.
The fleet session held its dispatch and cancelled 12 of its own queued runs at 21:35Z, but the hold expired at 22:29Z before pm-cli's jobs had started. At 23:01Z I cancelled 15 fleet feature-branch pull_request runs (no release, push, schedule, dispatch or Dependabot runs). After PR 1714 merged at 00:35Z on 2026-11-13, I re-ran the 6 whose PR head was unchanged; the other 9 had been superseded by newer pushes. Jobs created later on other repositories started before pm-cli's earlier-created jobs, so per-label queueing across repositories is not FIFO by creation time. A hold that ends at a fixed time therefore does not protect a PR whose fan-out starts late.
